packets.title: Slot 39 PLAYER_CAREER_LOGS (69K Records) Composite Indexing & Schema
packets.core_problem: Slot 39 contains 69,040 52-byte records, representing year-by-year career historical stats. How does the game index into this massive pool from Slot 1 (PLAYER)? Is there a start_log_index and log_count in Slot 1, or is Slot 39 sorted by PlayerID and SeasonYear?
packets.disassembly_anchor: Getter RVA 0xF400A0 accesses [rax + 0x270] (count) and [rax + 0x278] (pData); stride imul is 52 (0x34).
packets.reproducible_conditions: Game process running (PID 1828); pData is live at 0x7FF4E76C5CE0.
packets.expected_decoded_shape: { player_id: uint16, season_year: uint16, team_id: uint8, games_played: uint8, games_started: uint8, minutes: uint16, pts: uint16, reb: uint16, ast: uint16, stl: uint16, blk: uint16, fgm: uint16, fga: uint16, ftm: uint16, fta: uint16, tpm: uint16, tpa: uint16 }
packets.verification_method: Verify whether decoding matches known historical records for Michael Jordan, LeBron James, Stephen Curry with 100% statistical fidelity.

packets.title: Slot 35 TEAM_FINANCIAL_LEDGER_BLOCK (4KB Block) Multi-Year Decomposition
packets.core_problem: Slot 35 allocates 4,020 bytes per team (112 records across 30 active + historical franchises). This massive block governs salary payroll, cash flow, revenue, luxury tax, and arena operations. What is the internal sub-struct layout of this 4KB block?
packets.disassembly_anchor: Getter RVA 0xF3C6B0 accesses [rax + 0x230] (count) and [rax + 0x238] (pData); stride is 4020 (0xFB4).
packets.expected_decoded_shape: { team_id: uint8, current_payroll: int64, projected_tax: int64, cash_balance: int64, ticket_revenue_projected: int64, multi_year_commitments: list[int64] }
packets.verification_method: Cross-reference decoded payroll and luxury tax against in-game GM front-office screen for Golden State Warriors (highest tax bill in 2021-22).

packets.title: Slot 42 DRAFT_ASSETS (32 Bytes) Traded Pick Protection Bitmask
packets.core_problem: Future draft pick trading in NBA2K22 allows protections (e.g. top-3 protected, lottery protected, pick swaps). How does the 32-byte record encode original owning team, current owning team, draft year, round, and condition/protection logic?
packets.disassembly_anchor: Getter RVA 0xF3C940 accesses [rax + 0x2A0] (count) and [rax + 0x2A8] (pData); stride is 32 (0x20).
packets.expected_decoded_shape: { asset_id: uint16, year: uint16, round: uint8, original_team_id: uint8, current_owner_team_id: uint8, is_swap: bool, protection_kind: enum, protection_range: uint8 }
packets.verification_method: Check traded pick assets against known 2021-22 real-world traded picks (e.g. Lakers 2022 first round pick owned by Pelicans).

packets.title: Slot 22 TEAM_ROTATION_TIMELINE (360 Bytes) 48-Minute Substitution Grid
packets.core_problem: Slot 22 represents coach rotation timelines (360 bytes per team). 360 = 15 players * 24 bytes, or 30 players * 12 bytes, or 48 minutes * 7.5 bytes? How does the timeline represent which 5 players are on the floor for each minute of the game?
packets.disassembly_anchor: Getter RVA 0xF3ED70 accesses [rax + 0x160] (count) and [rax + 0x168] (pData); stride is 360 (0x168).
packets.expected_decoded_shape: { team_id: uint8, player_minutes_targets: list[uint8, 15], minute_by_minute_lineup: list[list[uint16, 5], 48] }
packets.verification_method: Compare decoded minute allocations with in-game Coach Rotation UI timeline.
